cards.explanation: The answer is False. The disciples did not know right away who He meant. "The disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to which of them He meant." They had no idea, friends. I think every one of them was checking every other face and hoping their own looked innocent.

The answer is to ask Jesus which one He means. Peter motioned to the disciple at Jesus' side to ask Jesus which one He was talking about. I think that's like a man trying to get a waiter's attention in a packed restaurant. Then the disciple leaned back and asked.

The answer is that Jesus gives that one a dipped morsel. Jesus answered, "It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it." Then He dipped the morsel and gave it away. The answer was a sign and not a name, and it was given right there at the table.
The answer is Judas. Jesus gave the dipped morsel to Judas son of Simon Iscariot. Judas is the disciple who kept the money bag (John 13:29). Right after he took it, Jesus spoke to him.

The answer is True. John 13:28 says, "But no one at the table knew why Jesus had said this to him." Not one person at the table knew why, friends. I think they were all just as lost as I am when somebody says "it's a quick fix" and hands me a wrench.

The answer is to buy what's needed for the feast. Because Judas kept the money bag, some thought Jesus was telling him "…to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor." Makes sense for a guy holding the cash. When I hear "go quickly," I figure it's a cookie run.

The answer is that he goes out into the night. "As soon as he had received the morsel, Judas went out into the night." The text says as soon as. This is one of the heavier lines in the passage, and I think it's okay to let it sit for a second.
The answer is False. Jesus says God "will glorify Him at once." There's no long wait in His words, friends. At once means right away, like when the timer goes off and you're already at the oven door.

The answer is that they cannot come there. Jesus says, "Where I am going, you cannot come." He had said the same thing to the Jews earlier. The disciples would look for Him, and this is what He tells them about where He's headed.

The answer is Love. Jesus says, "A new commandment I give you: Love one another." It's a short sentence, but it's the one He chose to give them right here at the table. I could stamp it on a whole batch.

The answer is the way He has loved them. Jesus says, "As I have loved you, so you also must love one another." He doesn't just give them the command. He points to how He has loved them as the example. That's a pretty high bar, friends, and it's the one He set.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another." Love is the thing that shows. I'd keep it simple too, since it's the one thing everybody can see.

The answer is "Lord, where are You going?" Simon Peter, one of the disciples, asks it. Jesus had just said they could not come where He was going. So Peter asks the question that was probably on everybody's mind. I think I'd have asked the same thing, only louder.

The answer is False. Peter does not stop there. He says, "Lord, why can't I follow You now?" He asks something more, friends. I'd have asked a lot of questions too, probably with my mustache flapping.

The answer is to lay down his life for Him. Peter says, "I will lay down my life for You." That's a huge promise to make, friends. Jesus answers it with a question, and the next lines show where it goes.

The answer is deny. Jesus says, "…before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." I think this one stings, and I'm not going to joke about it. Peter had just promised everything, and Jesus told him what was coming.
